selected_need: Extend QIF into a discovery and application runtime
intended_user_or_segment: Organizations that need to extract quality knowledge from experts or history and then apply it to real targets without domain-specific tooling assumptions
context_summary: QIF v0.1 and the expert-judgment baseline define knowledge structures, but runtime visibility is missing between elicitation, applicability selection, evidence collection, and verdict production.
hypothesis: A v0.2 runtime package set can make discovery and application inspectable through discovery sessions, quality culture aggregation, evaluation targets, applicability rules, and review runs.
rejected_alternatives: Assume software-development artifacts as the default target model.
Treat checklist completion as sufficient runtime evidence.
explicit_risks: Runtime artifacts may drift into software-specific assumptions unless target and applicability models stay domain-general.
delivery_validation_requirements: Run local validators against discovery, culture, target, and review-run packages and verify governance triggers on low-confidence conflict.
need: Show how quality knowledge is discovered and applied in a real QIF runtime.
intent: Add runtime models, schemas, examples, verifier rules, changelog, and AOF evidence for end-to-end discovery and application.
context: The repository already has operational and expert-judgment baselines; v0.2 must remain domain-general and non-surveillant while making verdict paths inspectable.
